correctness.rationale: For algebraically closed k of char p>=3 and ordinary elliptic E,Y, the assumed Cartier-logarithmic criterion reduces the specified normalized foliation 1-form to dlog g on Y with nonzero F_p residues at reduced poles. Residue sum=0 by the residue theorem; lifting residues to an integer degree-zero divisor Delta and factoring [p]=V∘F associates every logarithmic derivative to a p-division class. V is a connected cyclic etale degree-p isogeny on ordinary elliptic Y. Pullback under weighted Abel map over ordered distinct poles stays connected: restriction to varying a single pole yields pullback along multiplication a1 prime to p, preserving surjectivity on the cyclic p quotient; deleting finite points does not disconnect. Quotient by free S_d action partitions by residue multisets, each stratum degree p*d!/prod(m_j!), and character orthogonality gives C_{p,d} and N_{p,d}. Independently enumerated residue vectors/multisets for p=3,5,7 and 2<=d<=5 verifying all formulas. This checks only arithmetic; geometric proof relies on the stated primary foliation criterion and standard isogeny facts, not finite experiments.
residual_risks: Residue-count spot checks do not verify the Cartier premise or geometric connectedness.

originality.rationale: Andreatta–Goren is the essential 2026 source for p-closed turbulent foliations, ordinary-elliptic Cartier criterion, reduced-pole existence and surrounding moduli; these are fully credited. What appears additional in the reviewed proof is the explicit connected Kummer parameter torsor for each residue multiset, all stratum degrees and the closed residue census. However the original primary text and its §2 moduli construction were not obtainable, and the abstract claims to determine moduli spaces: an important specific priority risk remains. Qualified best-of-knowledge, not categorical whole-document noncoverage.
